content.title: About
content.content: Fried shrimp are a seafood product made from boiled or raw shrimp that are then deep‑fried until golden and crispy. They have a tender, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture. Fried shrimp are often served as an appetizer, added to salads, pastas, rice dishes, and sushi.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp belong to the crustacean family and are close relatives of lobsters and crayfish.
There are more than 2,000 shrimp species, but culinary use focuses on tiger, northern, and king shrimp.
Frying in oil preserves most of the protein while adding a rich flavor.
Shrimp can change color from gray to pink depending on the cooking method.
In Japan, fried shrimp are frequently served with soy sauce and wasabi.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Shrimp provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, making them an excellent source of high‑quality protein.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When fried moderately, the fat content remains low and is mostly polyunsaturated.

items.title: Source of iodine and selenium
items.content: Iodine supports thyroid function, while selenium has antioxidant properties.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids in shrimp help lower triglyceride levels.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Potential toxins
items.content: Improperly stored or undercooked shrimp can harbor bacteria and toxins.

items.title: High sodium in processed products
items.content: Pre‑packaged fried shrimp are often salted; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fried shrimp hot as a snack, add them to salads, pastas, rice bowls, tacos, or use them in sushi. They are easy to eat by hand, peeling off the tail, and the meat can be lifted from the shell with a fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fried shrimp in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a zip‑top bag at –18 °C. Before eating, check for any ammonia‑like or off odors.
